info.title: dotk.name API
info.description: The `.k` name registry on Kaspa. A name or key answer carries its deed address and the registry covenant id, so a caller can check it with one UTXO query to a Kaspa node.

get.summary: Get the cards a spender can sweep

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The previous page's `next`. Absent for the first page.

200.description: Success. A page of the unswept cards naming the spender, live or retired, with `next` while more follow. A spender with none answers an empty list, never 404

400.description: Not a key-owned scheme, not a 32-byte hex payload, or an `after` or `limit` this operation refuses

BlockRef.description: The last fully processed chain block.

CardChange.description: What an event did to a name's card.

CardOut.description:
One card: a name's records, as the indexer observed them minted.

The indexer proves nothing about a card. A reader proves one against its own node: a live
UTXO sits at `cardAddress`, that UTXO is output 1 of the transaction that created the deed's
current UTXO, `blob` hashes to `recordsHash`, and `blob` is at most 16 KiB. The indexer checks
the last two before it serves a card.

blob.description: The record blob, hex, in deterministic CBOR.

cardAddress.description: The card's P2SH address, where its UTXO sits.

live.description:
Whether the card speaks for its name now. Always true on a name or owner lookup. A
spender lookup also lists retired cards, which are left to sweep.

name.description:
The bare name the card's key belongs to. Absent only on a spender lookup where the key
has no row.

records.description:
The decoded blob: ENSIP-5 text records, local flags such as `primary`, and opaque values
that a client keeps. Absent when the blob is not a record map.

recordsHash.description: `blake3(blob)`, the hash the card's redeem script commits to.

spenderType.description: The key that can sweep the card: a key-owned scheme byte, its payload, and the address.

DayCount.description: One UTC day and how many names were registered on it.

day.description: The day in `YYYY-MM-DD`, UTC, from the accepting block's header timestamp.

DeedOut.description:
One deed: the state its address hashes from, plus the provenance the indexer observed.

The address hashes from `status ‖ key ‖ ownerType ‖ owner ‖ name`, with `key` and the padded
`name` taken from the enclosing `KeyResponse`. An ACTIVE deed carries `ownerType` and
`owner`. A PENDING deed carries `claim` instead, because its owner slot holds the claim hash.

acceptedDaa.description:
DAA score of the block that accepted the deed's split. It carries through activate and
transfer, so it is the registration time, and a PENDING deed is evictable at
`acceptedDaa + params.t_evict` from `/genesis`. Always present on a PENDING deed. Absent on an ACTIVE deed whose
registration this indexer did not observe.

claim.description:
PENDING only: the claim hash the split committed to. An evict needs it to rebuild
`{PENDING, key, 0x00, claim, zero}`, and nothing public reveals it.

deedAddress.description:
Where this deed lives: `P2SH(deed template ‖ the state above)`. A caller probes it against
its own node.

outpointIndex.description: Output index of the deed UTXO as last observed.

outpointTxid.description:
Transaction of the deed UTXO as last observed. Absent when this indexer never observed
the split, or when the chain refuted its claim.

ownerType.description: ACTIVE only: the KCC-2 scheme byte and the owner payload it names.

status.description:
The on-chain status that the address hashes from. Derive an address from this, never
from `kind`.

DeedStatus.description: The on-chain status of a deed.

ErrorCode.description:
Why a request failed, as a closed set a client can branch on instead of parsing `error`.
Each code implies its HTTP status.

code.description: One of a closed set, for branching.

error.description: The same failure in prose, for a person. Never parsed.

prev.description: The deed pre-image. Absent means the row did not exist before the event.

prevCards.description:
`existed: false` for a mint, which undo deletes. Otherwise the `sweptAt` the row carried
before the event.

prevGaps.description:
Pre-images of the gap rows the event wrote. An entry without `hi` means no row existed
at that `lo`, and undo deletes it. A split always creates one, so a journal without these
cannot undo a split.

GapOut.description:
One gap: the open interval `(lo, hi)` of unregistered keyspace, hex. Its P2SH address hashes
from these two bounds.

GapsByWidth.description:
Gap widths as multiples of the average gap, so the shape stays comparable as the registry
grows. With uniform keys it decays exponentially.

bucketsPerAverage.description: How many buckets span one average gap: 4, so each is a quarter of it.

counts.description:
Gaps per bucket, narrowest first. Bucket `i` holds the gaps at least
`i / bucketsPerAverage` and under `(i + 1) / bucketsPerAverage` times the average.

wider.description: Gaps wider than the last bucket. Not part of `counts`.

caughtUp.description:
Whether the indexer is caught up with the chain now: `lastBlock` is under 10 s old and under
60 s of blocks behind `tipBlueScore - tipDistance`. Never latched. `healthy` tolerates
10 s of `false`.

historySeq.description:
The registry's change marker, or `null` before any event. Poll it to
decide whether to re-read `/snapshot`. Compare for difference, not order, because a reorg
can lower it.

journalCoverage.description:
Lowest blue score the journal can undo exactly. 0 means full coverage. `null` only after
an import without a journal, until this process journals a block of its own.

netBps.description: The network's nominal blocks per second.

network.description:
The network the manifest was deployed on. With `registryCovenantId`, it identifies the
registry.

ownerUnknown.description: Rows whose key is proven registered but whose owner is refuted or was never observed.

registryCovenantId.description:
Which registry this indexer serves. A client compares it with its own pinned id before it
acts on any answer.

oneOf.description: The last self-test's verdict, or `null` before the first run has finished.

selfTestDetail.description: Where that run failed, present only for `?detail=true` and only once a run has finished.

tipBlueScore.description:
The sink's blue score as last observed, or `null` before the first observation.
`(tipBlueScore - tipDistance - lastBlock.blueScore) / netBps` is how many seconds behind
this indexer is. It freezes during a node outage, so the lag then reads low.

tipDistance.description:
Confirmation depth in blue score. The indexer does not read the chain blocks within this
distance below the tip.

HistoryEntry.description:
One event on a key, and the deed's state right after it. `kind` is absent when the event
ended the deed (a release or an evict).

blockTime.description: Header timestamp of the accepting chain block, in ms.

blueScore.description: Blue score of the accepting chain block.

cardChange.description: Absent when the event left the records alone.

claim.description: PENDING only: the claim hash the split committed to.

daaScore.description: DAA score of the accepting chain block, the clock every age in this API uses.

kind.description: The row's kind after the event. Absent when the deed ended here.

owner.description:
The KCC-2 owner payload, hex. Present only when the entry left the deed ACTIVE. No
address is served, because a client derives it from the pair.

seq.description: Apply order within the accepting block.

txid.description: The transaction that made the change.

HistoryOp.description:
What an event did to a key. A `sweep` spends a card on its own and leaves the deed
unchanged.

HistoryResponse.description:
One key's history, newest first, one page at a time.

It holds only what this indexer observed. Kaspa prunes old blocks, so that can be less than
the full past, and `complete` says which it is.

complete.description:
Whether the oldest entry held is the key's own registration. `false` for an empty
history too.

KeyKind.description: A row's kind, or `free` for a key without a row.

KeyResponse.description:
Everything a client needs to act on one key: its deed and the gaps a transaction touching it
must co-spend.

covering.description: `free` only: the gap that strictly contains the key, which a split spends.

deed.description: The key's own deed. Absent for `free` and `ownerUnknown`.

kind.description:
The indexer's row knowledge. This is not the on-chain status. Read `deed.status` to
derive an address.

name.description: The bare name. Absent when the row has none, which is always the case for PENDING.

neighbours.description:
Occupied keys only: the two gaps flanking the key. With the deed, they are all a release
needs. Never present together with `covering`.

proven.description:
Whether the last self-test passed and left no blind spot around this key. This is
coverage, not freshness: it is as old as that self-test, which finished at `provenAt`. A
client can probe the deed address itself.

KeysByPrefix.description:
Registered keys per leading key byte: 256 buckets per array, in order. Kinds stay separate,
so each client chooses which to merge. Merging adjacent buckets gives the exact histogram
over one bit less of prefix.

KeyspaceResponse.description:
The whole keyspace at a glance: two distributions and their totals. Always a live database
read and never proven, so it carries no `proven`.

oneOf.description: The last processed chain block, which is what this answer is current to.

registrationsByDay.description:
Registrations per UTC day, oldest first, only days with at least one. Counted from
`register` events, so a name released or evicted since still counts.

KeyspaceTotals.description: Registry totals. The deed counts are sums of `keysByPrefix`, so they always agree with it.

gaps.description:
Live gaps, counted independently. The partition invariant makes this deeds + 1, so a
client can check it.

allOf.description: Fields this build does not know.

deedTemplateHash.description: The same for the deed template.

gapAbi.description: The gap covenant's ABI artifact: bytecode, state span, dispatch tags and argument types.

gapTemplateHash.description: A client that rebuilds the gap template and gets another hash refuses the manifest.

genesisBinding.description:
The covenant id's full preimage: the outpoint the deployer spent, which output was the
genesis gap, and that output with its redeem script and state. A client can recompute the
id and check the genesis output group had exactly one member, with no chain access.

network.description: The Kaspa network this registry was deployed on.

params.description:
The protocol parameters compiled into the templates, so a forged copy yields addresses
that hold no UTXO.

version.description: Manifest shape version. A client refuses a version it does not read.

Manifest.description:
The deployment manifest, byte for byte as built into this indexer.

Unknown fields stay open, because the manifest is relayed verbatim and newer tooling can add
fields. `gapAbi` and `deedAbi` are open objects, because their shape belongs to silverscript.

address.description: The owner as a Kaspa address. Absent only for a covenant-id owner (0x04).

card.description: The name's live card, if it has one.

deedAddress.description: A UTXO at this address carrying `registryCovenantId` proves this answer.

name.description: The bare canonical name that the key hashes from, without the display suffix `.k`.

owner.description: The raw owner payload, hex. For every scheme but 0x04 it is the owner address's payload.

NeighbourGaps.description:
The two gaps flanking a live key. The predecessor leads at merge seat 0 (`merge`) and the
successor delegates at seat 2 (`absorbed`). Swapping them builds a transaction the covenant
rejects.

OwnerResponse.description:
Every live name one owner holds. The owner is the `(ownerType, owner)` pair a deed stores,
and `address` is that pair as a Kaspa address.

address.description: The owner as a Kaspa address. Absent only for a covenant-id owner (0x04).

cards.description: The live card of each name that has one.

names.description: Every live name this owner holds that the last self-test proved.

OwnerType.description: The owner scheme byte in decimal: 0 p2pk-schnorr, 3 p2sh, 4 covenant, 133/134 p2pk-ecdsa.

RecordValue.description:
A record value: text for ENSIP-5 keys, a flag for a local key such as `primary`, or an
opaque value (one CBOR item as hex) that a client writes back unchanged.

bridged.description: Registered keys the table lacked, adopted as owner-unknown.

cardsRestored.description: Card rows the probe marked unswept again.

cardsSwept.description: Card rows the probe marked swept. Not a verdict input.

demoted.description: Rows with refuted ownership, kept as owner-unknown.

dropped.description: Rows removed because the chain shows their key unregistered.

gapsSynced.description: Gap cache rows adopted, corrected or dropped. Not a verdict input.

iterations.description: Passes the repair took to converge.

readopted.description: Registered keys the table lacked, adopted with their proven state.

rewritten.description: Rows whose outpoint, value and acceptance DAA were rewritten from the observed UTXO.

RowKind.description: The indexer's knowledge of a row. `ownerUnknown` has no on-chain counterpart.

SelfTestDetail.description:
What the last self-test could not prove, and what repair did, served only for
`?detail=true`. Each list holds at most 100 entries, and the `…Omitted` field beside it
counts the rest.

blindSpots.description:
Residual blind spots after repair, as [lo, hi] hex key brackets: keyspace whose
registrations this indexer never observed, or a gap that failed only the last probe.

failingOutpoints.description:
Outpoints that failed 3 times in a row or only the last probe, as `outpoint:<hex key>`.
Failing gaps and deeds appear in `blindSpots` and `ownerUnknown` instead.

ownerUnknown.description:
Registered rows whose deed address is refuted, as [hex key, name]. Repair demotes these
to owner-unknown, so an entry here means the pipeline kept touching the row or the
refutation came only in the last probe.

pendingChecked.description:
How many of `deedsChecked` were PENDING deeds. This counts what the run proved, where
`/health`'s `pending` counts what the table holds now.

published.description: Whether this run refreshed the `/snapshot` proof.

repaired.description:
What repair did: rows dropped, demoted, re-adopted, bridged or rewritten, plus gap cache
rows reconciled.

SelfTestSummary.description:
The last self-test's verdict, served on every `/health`. The failure coordinates are in
`SelfTestDetail`, served only on request, because pages poll this body.

deedsChecked.description:
Deed addresses confirmed. Lower than the row count when owner-unknown rows exist, because
those have no address to derive.

finishedMs.description: Wall-clock unix ms at which the run ended.

gapsChecked.description: Derived gaps confirmed against the UTXO set: the completeness half of the proof.

startedMs.description: Wall-clock unix ms at which the run started.

Snapshot.description:
The registry for mirrors and bootstrap. The canonical core is `registryCovenantId` and the
key-sorted `deeds`. The resume section is `vcpCheckpoint` and `events`, the journal tail.

cards.description:
Unswept cards only. Cards are outside the canonical core, and the self-test proves
nothing about them.

historySeq.description:
The `historySeq` that `/health` publishes, read in the same transaction as the rows.
It tells a polling client which registry state it received. History ids are local to one
indexer, so this is outside the canonical core, and an importer ignores it.

proven.description:
Set by the self-test that proved this snapshot against the UTXO set. This field and
`provenAt` are outside the canonical core, and an importer ignores both.

SpenderCardsResponse.description: The unswept cards naming one spender, live or retired, so a wallet can find cards to reclaim.

next.description: The `after` of the next page, `{txid}:{index}`. Absent on the last page.

SpenderType.description: A key-owned scheme byte in decimal: 0 p2pk-schnorr, 133/134 p2pk-ecdsa.
